answer: One concrete defense is stake plus slow reputation: an agent must lock collateral and build a verifiable work history before transacting at full weight. A new identity starts at the horizon of trust, limited to small tasks. Reputation then grows like a glacier — each honest job adds a little weight, and fraud triggers slashing. To reach the summit of influence, an attacker must fund thousands of stakes and sustain months of honest work per identity, so the cost of a fake army exceeds the profit from rigging any single market.
